- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.22) within 5 days of forecast, reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak or neutral (0.00–0.11) and recent price is trending down; add 1–2% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; apply 2-period lag correction: if true outcome drops 2% from prior, forecast should not exceed prior minus 1.5%.
- When sentiment history shows repeated +0.11/0.17 patterns, model tends to overfit upward trend; apply downward bias correction of 0.5–1.5% per 3-day sentiment window.
